pages.title: Kitchens
pages.content:
Eight kitchens cook under the one roof, each with its own counter, its own cook and its own three lunch plates. Take a tray from the rail, order at as many counters as you like, and carry everything to a long shared table.

Ladle Lane

Noodle soups led by Tomás Ferreira: clear chicken noodle soup, sesame broth with greens, cold noodles with herbs.

Ember Grill

Charcoal flatbreads and skewers led by Amara Osei: flatbread with grilled squash, a chicken skewer plate, yoghurt and herb dip.

Green Counter

Grain bowls and salads led by Lena Kowalski: barley bowl, roast roots and lentils, seasonal leaves.

Wok Row

Wok-fried rice and greens led by Daniel Cho: egg fried rice, charred greens, pepper tofu.

Spice Shelf

Curries led by Priya Nair: lentil dal, chickpea and spinach curry, rice with pickles.

Fresca

Fresh pasta led by Marco Bellini: tagliatelle with tomato, ricotta ravioli, bean and pasta soup.

Bakehouse

Breads and soups led by Ingrid Holm: soup and rye bread, cheese toastie, cardamom bun.

Steep

Coffee, tea and small sweets, run by the hall team and led by Ruth Adeyemi: filter coffee, black tea, almond cake.

pages.title: Lunch Hour
pages.content:
Weekday lunch runs from 11:00 to 15:00, with the last lunch order at 14:30 and the peak between 12:10 and 13:00.

How the hour runs

11:00, doors open; trays, water and cutlery set on the rail. 11:45, early tables fill and the kitchens fire their first bowls. 12:10, the peak begins: held tables are seated first and the queue moves by kitchen. 13:00, second wave; tables turn and coffee starts at Steep. 14:30, last lunch order; the hall quietens for slow eaters.

The hall resets at 15:00 and the evening kitchens open at 17:00, with the last tables at 21:30.

pages.title: Hold a Table
pages.content:
Holding a table costs nothing. Write or call the hall by 11:00 with your time and party size (tables seat 2 to 12), and the hall team confirms. Your table is marked with a wooden block and kept for 15 minutes past the booked time.

Groups of 6 to 12 book 24 hours ahead and can take the Group lunch set at €18.00 per person.

Write to hello@hiroba-hall.example or call +31 10 555 0190.

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Hiroba Food Hall, Havenhof 12, 3011 AB Rotterdam, Netherlands, on the ground floor of a former harbour warehouse.

Open Monday to Friday 11:00 to 21:30 and Saturday 12:00 to 21:30; closed on Sunday. Lunch service runs 11:00 to 15:00 with the last lunch order at 14:30.

Take tram 8 to Havenhof, then walk four minutes. There are 60 bicycle racks and no car park.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
Hiroba Food Hall opened on 4 March 2019 on the ground floor of a former harbour warehouse in Rotterdam, with eight independent kitchens, 180 seats at long shared tables and a counter of 24 stools.

The hall is built around one idea: that a weekday lunch should be calm, shared and fast without being rushed. Guests take a tray along the rail, choose from several counters, and sit together.

Ruth Adeyemi has managed the hall since opening day. “We set the pace of the room around 12:10,” she says. “Everything else follows from that.”

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Write to Hiroba Food Hall at hello@hiroba-hall.example or call +31 10 555 0190. The hall team, led by Ruth Adeyemi, answers during hall hours: Monday to Friday 11:00 to 21:30 and Saturday 12:00 to 21:30.

Hiroba Food Hall, Havenhof 12, 3011 AB Rotterdam, Netherlands.

posts.title: A table for twelve on a Thursday
posts.excerpt: How a team of twelve gets one long table, one tray each and a lunch that starts on time.
posts.content:
A team of twelve wrote to the hall on Tuesday evening. By Wednesday morning we had confirmed a table by the window, marked it with a wooden block and told the kitchens to expect them at 12:30.

On Thursday they arrived together, found the block, and split up along the rail: noodles at Ladle Lane, curry at Spice Shelf, flatbreads from Ember Grill. Twelve trays were back at one table within ten minutes.

Groups of 6 to 12 book 24 hours ahead and can take the Group lunch set at €18.00 per person. The table is held for 15 minutes past the booked time, and holding it costs nothing.

posts.title: Two kitchens on one tray
posts.excerpt: The two-kitchen tray: half portions from two counters, carried to the table together.
posts.content:
The two-kitchen tray is the hall’s quietest idea. You take half a portion from one kitchen and half from another, and they travel on a single tray for €14.00.

A favourite pairs a small bowl of clear chicken noodle soup from Ladle Lane with flatbread and yoghurt dip from Ember Grill. The cooks at the pass keep the portions even.

Ask at either counter; there is nothing to book.

posts.title: What 12:10 looks like from the pass
posts.excerpt: Tomás Ferreira on the minutes when the queue turns and the first big wave arrives.
posts.content:
At 12:10 the first big wave reaches Ladle Lane. Tomás Ferreira has been at the pot since early morning and by now the broth is exactly where he wants it.

“You stop looking at the queue and start looking at the tickets,” he says. Held tables are seated first, the queue moves by kitchen, and the rail keeps trays flowing.

By 13:00 the second wave comes in, tables turn and coffee starts at Steep.

posts.title: Why the hall resets at three
posts.excerpt: Ruth Adeyemi on the afternoon pause between lunch and the evening kitchens.
posts.content:
After the last lunch order at 14:30 the hall quietens for slow eaters. At 15:00 the tables are wiped, the rail is cleared and the cooks take a breath.

Ruth Adeyemi, hall manager since 2019, calls it the hall’s second breakfast: a short reset before the evening kitchens open at 17:00.

Coffee and tea from Steep are served through the afternoon.
